rows.author: C013
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 2 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1405, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"SECRECY OF BANK DEPOSITS LAW,\" EXEMPTING GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES FROM THE PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCLOSURE OF OR INQUIRY INTO DEPOSITS WITH ANY BANKING INSTITUTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to exempt government officials and employees, whether elected or appointed, from the coverage of the Bank Secrecy Law in order to equip law enforcement authorities with the tools needed to go after crooks in government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-11-17

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING LATE REGISTRANTS TO REGISTER THEIR BIRTH IN THE OFFICE OF THE LOCAL CIVIL REGISTRAR OF EITHER THE PLACE OF THEIR RESIDENCE OR THE PLACE OF THEIR BIRTH
rows.abstract: The bill allows late registrants to register their birth at the Office of the Local Civil Registrar in either the place of their birth or their present residence. The later registrant must submit the following documents: a) a declaration by either parent, relative or any person who has knowledge of the birth of the late registrant; and b) an affidavit explaining the delayed registration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING THE AMOUNT OF ONE BILLION PESOS FROM THE AGGREGATE EARNINGS OF THE PHILIPPINE AMUSEMENT AND GAMING CORPORATION
rows.abstract: The bill provides for an additional funding of P1.0 billion for the maintenance and operation of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE METRO CEBU TRAFFIC AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-10

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE POSSESSION OR USE OF MOBILE OR CELLULAR TELEPHONE BY CONVICTED PRISONERS AND INDIVIDUALS WHILE INCARCERATED AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill bans the possession or use of cellular telephones by convicted prisoners and individuals while they are incarcerated in detention centers; in provincial, city or municipal jails; or in national penal institutions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SALARIES TO BARANGAY TANODS, MEMBERS OF THE LUPONG TAGAPAMAYAPA, AND BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The bill grants a P500 monthly compensation to barangay tanods, members of the lupong tagapamayapa and barangay health workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT ONLY PROOF OF OWNERSHIP SHALL BE REQUIRED IN SHIPPING ANY MOTOR VEHICLE, MOTOR VEHICLE ENGINE, ENGINE BLOCK, CHASSIS, OR BODY FROM ONE ISLAND TO ANOTHER, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"ANTI-CARNAPPING ACT OF 1972\"
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to eliminate the Philippine National Police clearance requirement for transporting a motor vehicle, motor engine, engine block, chassis or body from one island to another.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES TO DRUG STORES WHICH REFUSE TO HONOR SENIOR CITIZEN CARDS ISSUED BY THE GOVERNMENT FOR AVAILMENT OF BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES GRANTED TO SENIOR CITIZENS
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to penalize drug stores, which refuse to honor the senior citizen's card, with a fine ranging from P1,000 to P5,000 or imprisonment from one month to six months.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2006-08-07

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2005-05-04

rows.title_short: The Land Administration Reform Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Land Administration Reform Act of 2004.\" The bill provides for the creation of the Land Administration Authority that shall be responsible for land administration and public land management. It also establishes the Land Adjudcation Board that will adjudicate land administration and public land management matters.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04846

rows.author: C069
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09344) enacted on 2006-04-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUVENILE JUSTICE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"The Juvenile Justice Act of 2001.\" The bill provides a just and more humane system of treating juvenile offenders with the aim in view of rehabilitating and reintegrating them into the mainstream of society. Creates the Office of the Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention to oversee the implementation of the act, and the Office of the Child Ombudsman to check and monitor its implementation.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05065

rows.status: Substituted by HB06027

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENSURE PUBLIC ACCESS TO OFFICIAL RECORDS, DOCUMENTS AND ANY OTHER INFORMATION OF PUBLIC CONCERN
rows.abstract: \"Freedom of Information Act.\" The bill provides for absolute and mandatory access to matters of official information, public concern and public interest. It mandates all government bodies to provide the requested information within five days from receipt of a written request.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06106

rows.abstract: \"GMO-Free Food and Agriculture Act of 2004.\" The bill aims to keep the country's food free from genetically modified organisms at this time when there are still unresolved questions as to their effects on human health and on the environment.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING TAX EXEMPTION, PRIVILEGES AND ASSISTANCE TO RURAL ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES AS A MATTER OF STATE POLICY TO AID THE PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION ON TOTAL ELECTRIFICATION
rows.abstract: The bill provides that for a period of 50 years from the date of cooperative organization as a non-stock entity operating as a public entity, rural electric cooperatives (RECs) shall be exempt from the payment of: a) all national and local taxes and fees including but not limited to franchise, realty and business taxes; and b) all duties or imposts on foreign materials, equipment and goods acquired for the operation of the RECs.

rows.abstract: The bill increases the excise tax rates imposed on alcohol and tobacco products by 18% over and above the mandated 12% increase provided under RA 8240. It provides for another 15% adjustment in the excise tax rates three years after the effectivity of the law.
